account: Shortly before 4 a.m. on Thursday 3 September 2026, Waymo pulled one of its driverless cars over in San Francisco's Richmond District. Waymo had detected a “violation of our terms of service involving a firearm”. The company alerted emergency services and “cooperated fully” with police, a Waymo spokesperson told the Los Angeles Times (12 September). The San Francisco Police Department said that officers made a “high-risk vehicle stop” and detained the two juvenile passengers. Officers found a loaded AR-style assault rifle, suspected marijuana and mace spray, and the two were taken to juvenile hall. The Independent, citing SFGATE, quotes police spokesperson Allison Maxie calling the weapon an “AR-styled assault rifle also known as a ghost gun”. It says that the boy and girl were booked into the Juvenile Justice Center on firearm-possession charges. The California Post puts the stop at 40th Avenue and Cabrillo Street. The Independent and Xataka both say that it is unclear how the firearm was detected. On 17 September 2026, Waymo spokesperson Julia Ilina told The Verge that the company uses automated technology to help its teams identify potential violations such as firearms inside the vehicle. She said that Waymo may contact local police when it detects a firearm. Waymo did not say whether software or staff flagged the weapon in this ride. It did not explain what role humans play between an automated alert and a call to police. No report through 29 October 2026 gives the outcome of the firearm charges against the two minors.

ai_role.statement: Waymo told The Verge that automated technology helps its teams identify potential violations such as a firearm in the cabin. Waymo did not say whether software or staff first flagged the weapon in this ride. It also did not explain how the system judges that an object may be a firearm or what role people play between an alert and a call to police. The driverless car pulled over, and police officers made the stop, the search and the arrests. In the July 2026 San Mateo case, Reason reports, citing NBC Bay Area, that a Waymo representative who was watching the live interior camera feeds called police.

fields.account: Shortly before 4 a.m. on Thursday 3 September 2026, Waymo pulled one of its driverless cars over in San Francisco's Richmond District. Waymo had detected a “violation of our terms of service involving a firearm”. The company alerted emergency services and “cooperated fully” with police, a Waymo spokesperson told the Los Angeles Times (12 September). The San Francisco Police Department said that officers made a “high-risk vehicle stop” and detained the two juvenile passengers. Officers found a loaded AR-style assault rifle, suspected marijuana and mace spray, and the two were taken to juvenile hall. The Independent, citing SFGATE, quotes police spokesperson Allison Maxie calling the weapon an “AR-styled assault rifle also known as a ghost gun”. It says that the boy and girl were booked into the Juvenile Justice Center on firearm-possession charges. The California Post puts the stop at 40th Avenue and Cabrillo Street. The Independent and Xataka both say that it is unclear how the firearm was detected. On 17 September 2026, Waymo spokesperson Julia Ilina told The Verge that the company uses automated technology to help its teams identify potential violations such as firearms inside the vehicle. She said that Waymo may contact local police when it detects a firearm. Waymo did not say whether software or staff flagged the weapon in this ride. It did not explain what role humans play between an automated alert and a call to police. No report through 29 October 2026 gives the outcome of the firearm charges against the two minors.
fields.summary: After Waymo detected a firearm violation, one of its driverless cars pulled over in San Francisco on 3 September 2026; police found a loaded ghost gun and booked two minors.

purpose: The Waymo Driver is built to provide driverless rides. The service's rider rules prohibit weapons, and Xataka says that interior cameras record rides so that the company can check compliance and respond to emergencies. Pulling over and calling police on a firearm violation is that safeguard at work.

ratings.reason: SFPD took a loaded AR-style ghost gun, suspected marijuana and mace from two juveniles. It booked both on firearm-possession charges after the company's alert, per the Los Angeles Times and The Independent.
A loaded unserialized rifle was taken out of circulation, and two minors were charged. No report shows a harm that was about to occur, so the public benefit is the seizure itself.
